The exact IRS_V technical-sheet file is titled “IRS 5” (the Roman-numeral model) and gives 15 Hz–45 kHz ±2 dB, 4 ohms nominal, and six 12-inch woofers per channel. The sheet describes a multi-module system with a per-channel driver list, an electronic crossover, and included 2 kW/channel RMS bass amplifiers. The driver list is system/channel-specific, so no whole-system driverCount is inferred; the bass-amplifier requirement is not stored as total speaker amplifier output or power handling, and active/passive remains N/A for this composite system. No raw response-point or polar dataset is supplied. Source: https://www.infinity-classics.de/technik/manuals/IRS_V_technical_sheet.pdf.

The Spendor SP-100 owner’s manual specifies one 300 mm Bextrene LF unit, one 160 mm midrange, and one 19 mm soft-dome HF unit (three drivers); 8 ohms nominal; 45 Hz–20 kHz ±3 dB; 90 dB at 1 W/1 m; and 125 W power handling (the manual does not label this RMS/continuous). The stored 11.81-inch woofer size is a direct unit conversion of the published 300 mm. Its tri-wire/external-amplifier connections identify a passive loudspeaker. The manual’s illustrative “typical loudspeaker response curve” is not a measured SP100 response dataset, so no points or directivity are imported. Source: https://manualmachine.com/spendor/sp100/2351828-owners-manual/.

Barefoot’s exact Footprint03 page calls it a true three-way active, tri-amplified monitor and lists 260 watts of power per monitor, 45 Hz–40 kHz frequency response, a 6.5-inch woofer, 3.5-inch midrange, and 1-inch ring-radiator tweeter (three drivers). The manufacturer does not state a frequency tolerance or whether the 260 W is RMS/continuous/peak; the power field is therefore explicitly amplifier output, with no further rating implied. Its 105 dB figure is maximum peak SPL, not sensitivity. No measured response points or polar data are supplied/imported. Source: https://barefootsound.com/footprint03/.

The exact PSB T600 specifications list an on-axis 0° response of 24 Hz–23 kHz ±3 dB, 4 ohms nominal and minimum, three 6.5-inch woofers plus one 5.25-inch midrange and one 1-inch tweeter (five drivers), 300 W program power, and 20–300 W recommended amplifier power (the latter range is not collapsed into a scalar). The source gives 89 dB anechoic and 91 dB listening-room sensitivity but no electrical reference, so sensitivity remains N/A. The off-axis 30° ±1.5 dB specification (30 Hz–10 kHz) is retained in notes only, not represented as a full polar curve. Stereophile published measured on/off-axis plots for this exact model as images, not a numeric response/polar dataset; nothing was digitized. Source: https://www.psbspeakers.com/products/synchrony-t600-tower ; measured-plot lead: https://www.stereophile.com/content/psb-synchrony-t600-loudspeaker-measurements.
